# Benchmarking Compact VLMs for Clip-Level Surveillance Anomaly Detection Under Weak Supervision
## 1. Introduction
### 1.3. Field Snapshot
LAVAD generates frame-level captions with a VLM and uses an LLM to temporally aggregate and score anomalies without any task-specific training [ [43](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12653427/#B43-jimaging-11-00400)], demonstrating competitive zero-training performance on UCF-Crime [ [6](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12653427/#B6-jimaging-11-00400)] and XD-Violence [ [14](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12653427/#B14-jimaging-11-00400)].

## 2. Materials and Methods
### 2.1. Data
UCF-Crime [ [6](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12653427/#B6-jimaging-11-00400)] is the sole dataset used in this study and serves as a standard benchmark for video anomaly detection; the task is framed as clip-level binary classification (normal vs. abnormal) with no temporal boundaries inside clips to keep the supervision and evaluation units aligned.

We convert each UCF-Crime [ [6](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12653427/#B6-jimaging-11-00400)] video into RGB clips using uniform temporal sampling with a variable number of frames: for videos under 60 s, frames are sampled at 0.5 fps across the full duration, while for longer videos, 32 frames are uniformly sampled over the entire timeline; no audio or optical flow is used.

UCF-Crime [ [6](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12653427/#B6-jimaging-11-00400)] was selected as the sole benchmark because it provides long, untrimmed CCTV videos across 13 crime categories and is the community standard for weakly supervised anomaly detection, aligning with a clip-level binary protocol and supporting reproducible comparisons.

web.title: Real-world Anomaly Detection in Surveillance Videos
web.description:
## Real-world Anomaly Detection in Surveillance Videos
Our experimental results show that our MIL method for anomaly detection achieves significant improvement on anomaly detection performance as compared to the state-of-the-art approaches.

In this work, we propose an anomaly detection algorithm using weakly labeled training videos.

Using both positive (anomalous) and negative (normal) bags, we train the anomaly detection model using the proposed deep MIL ranking loss.

**UCF-Crime Dataset**

We construct a new large-scale dataset, called UCF-Crime, to evaluate our method. For more details about the UCF-Crime dataset, please refer to our paper.

# Video Anomaly Detection: An Introduction
## UCF-Crime
UCF-Crime dataset ( [Sultani et al., 2018](https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04264)) is an early large-scale VAD dataset capturing realistic anomalies. 6.

![](https://miro.medium.com/v2/resize:fit:700/1*nVgWJ4kXGfpRZWUQLANcBg.png)

## XD-Violence
Different from other datasets, XD-Violence ( [Wu et al., 2020](https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.04687)) is a large-scale VAD dataset providing 4,754 untrimmed videos with audio signals, allowing models to leverage multimodal information for anomaly detection.
